messages:
incident_bot: Pager alert -> Dedicated pool 'orpheus-enterprise-prod' (VPC) GPU utilization 98% for 3m, queueing rising, possible tenant starvation. Paging on-call.

alice_oncall: on it. looking at metrics now — joining grafana.

sam_sre: seeing sustained 98-100% across all 8 GPUs. kernel queue length up, avg latency for tenant requests jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s, error 503s climbing.

jesse_pm: customer (Orpheus Inc) just opened a support ticket: "inference timeouts affecting checkout flow".

rick_support: confirmed ticket. They said spike started ~10:02am UTC. They call this "checkout latency" — high business impact.

mara_eng: checked model versions — orpheus pinned to rwd-encoder-v2@sha123. No deploys in last 24h from their side. Could be query pattern change.

alice_oncall: load by endpoint: their /chat endpoint is 87% of tokens. Each request concurrency spiked. Avail capacity in pool = 0. Autoscale policy min=8, max=12 but scale-up lag ~6-8m.

sam_sre: options: 1) wait for autoscale (8->10) — will take ~6m; 2) enable burst to shared-hosted capacity (immediate but requires manual approval for cost); 3) evict low-priority tenants in this dedicated cluster (we have a couple non-critical warm jobs).

jesse_pm: customer SLA critical. Recommend immediate burst + temporary throttling on their non-essential endpoints. Need cost approval.

alice_oncall: I can initiate burst override. per-runbook: `redwoodctl pools burst --pool orpheus-enterprise-prod --duration 45m --approve-by oncall`

mara_eng: before burst, can we reduce per-request concurrency by adjusting worker_concurrency on the runtime for that tenant? Quick patch: `redwoodctl tenants update --tenant orpheus --runtime-config "concurrency=2"` — will lower throughput but help with queueing.

rick_support: Orpheus contact on the call: they prefer we keep checkout latency low; they're ok with temporary rate limits if we notify them.

alice_oncall: starting with immediate measures: 1) enable burst to shared-hosted now (I have approvals), 2) apply concurrency=2 for their runtime, 3) place 10% throttling on non-critical endpoints. Executing.

incident_bot: Action initiated: burst-request id=br-7723, status=IN_PROGRESS.

sam_sre: burst accepted by infra, adding 4 GPU-equivalents from shared pool. Pool capacity now 12/12 available for assignment. Watch latency.

mara_eng: applied `concurrency=2` to tenant runtime. Confirmed change on runtime-config.

alice_oncall: applying throttle rule for endpoints: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/pools/orpheus/rates -d '{"endpoint":"/chat","limit":80}'` -> deployed.

jesse_pm: notified the customer about temporary throttling + burst. They acknowledged and asked for ETA to return to normal.

sam_sre: metrics: token latency dropped to 320ms median within 90s of burst. 503s down to near zero. Queue length reducing.

rick_support: customer reported immediate improvement. Thanks.

laura_reliability: taking over escalation for the next shift. handoff: incident state = active-mitigation, burst br-7723 until +45m, concurrency override in place, rate-limit applied. Will monitor.

alice_oncall: leaving notes in incident channel and opening postmortem ticket. Assigning mara_eng + sam_sre + laura_reliability for RCA. Ticket: PM-INC-8712.

mara_eng: quick root theories: 1) query pattern spike (higher token per request) 2) model change client-side causing longer decode steps 3) background batch jobs hitting same pool. Need request logs and tenant metrics to validate.

jesse_pm: we'll request Orpheus to share any client-side changes and provide sample trace.

laura_reliability: next steps for followup: - keep burst active until autoscale stabilizes or until we add permanent capacity - run a token-cost and concurrency analysis - prepare rollback plan for burst (auto if not needed) - schedule postmortem meeting.

incident_bot: Pager resolved for oncall alice_oncall (ack at 1799912348).

alice_oncall: handing off to laura_reliability. leaving runbook snippet: ```Runbook: if dedicated pool exhausts -> enable burst, reduce concurrency, throttle non-critical, notify customer, open RCA ticket.```

laura_reliability: thanks. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. Closing Slack thread when ticket created and customer confirm.

rick_support: customer confirmed checkout flow restored. Closing loop.

mara_eng: creating data dump for postmortem (logs, sample requests, gpu metrics).

laura_reliability: postmortem owner assigned to mara_eng. ETA draft within 48h.

jesse_pm: summary: burst enabled -> immediate relief, temp concurrency + rate limit applied, customer impact mitigated. RCA in progress.

incident_bot: Thread closed (automated) at 1799912700."
